learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how to organize numerical data in grids, perform automated calculations using Formulas and Functions, and visualize data using Charts.

key_vocabulary.definition: A software application used to organize, analyze, and store data in a tabular format (rows and columns).
The intersection of a row and a column where data is entered.
A mathematical equation created by the user to perform calculations (e.g., =A1+B1).
A built-in, pre-defined formula in the spreadsheet software (e.g., =SUM(A1:A5)).

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A 'Workbook' is the entire file (like a notebook). A 'Worksheet' is a single page inside that workbook containing a grid of cells. Columns are labeled with letters (A, B, C) and Rows with numbers (1, 2, 3).

Every cell has an address (e.g., C4 means Column C, Row 4). A 'Range' is a group of cells (e.g., A1:A5 means all cells from A1 down to A5). 'Relative Referencing' changes the cell address when you copy a formula. 'Absolute Referencing' (using $ like $A$1) locks the address so it doesn't change.

Every formula or function MUST start with an equals sign (=). Basic math uses operators (+, -, *, /). Built-in functions make complex math easy: =SUM() adds numbers, =AVERAGE() finds the mean, =MAX() finds the highest number, and =MIN() finds the lowest.
Spreadsheets can instantly turn boring numbers into colorful visual graphs. Bar/Column charts compare items, Line charts show trends over time, and Pie charts show percentages of a whole.

fun_activity.title: 🧮 The Equal Sign Rule
fun_activity.instructions: Open Excel/Calc. Type `5+5` in a cell and press Enter. What happens? Nothing, it just says '5+5'. Now type `=5+5` and press Enter. Boom, it says '10'! The equal sign `=` is the magic key that tells the software: 'Stop treating this as text and do the math!'

exam_tips: 📌 Always start your formula syntax with an `=` sign in exam answers. (e.g., `=SUM(B2:B10)`).
📌 Distinguish between Relative and Absolute referencing. Use the dollar sign `$` to explain absolute reference (e.g., locking the GST rate cell).
📌 A formula is user-defined (`=A1*B1`), while a function is a pre-defined word (`=SUM()`).
quick_recap: ⭐ The currently selected cell is called the 'Active Cell' and is highlighted by a thick border.
⭐ A group of continuous cells selected together is called a Cell Range.
⭐ Charts make complex numerical data easy to understand at a glance.
